How We Rate
Licence and legal entity checks
We read the footer of each casino site, note the stated licensing authority and the registered company behind the domain, then check whether that licence is presented clearly or buried. We treat an unverifiable or vaguely worded licence statement as a mark against a site rather than a neutral detail.
Terms read in full, not just headlines
Every bonus claim is checked against the published terms. We look for wagering multipliers, whether the requirement applies to deposit plus bonus, game contribution tables, maximum bonus bets, expiry windows and cashout caps. Where terms are missing or contradictory, we say so instead of assuming the best case.
Payments and GBP handling
We record which deposit and withdrawal methods are listed, stated minimums, any fees and whether accounts can be held in pounds sterling. Deposit availability is assessed separately from withdrawal availability, because the two lists rarely match on gambling sites not on GamStop.
Withdrawal conditions and verification
We separate the operator's own approval or pending period from the time a bank, card scheme or wallet takes to settle. We also note published identity verification and source-of-funds requirements, withdrawal caps per day, week or month, and any conditions that pause a payout.
Games, providers and RTP transparency
We look at the breadth of slots, table games and live dealer rooms, which studios supply them, and whether the casino publishes return to player figures per title. A long provider logo strip is not treated as evidence of quality; configurable RTP versions and missing game information are noted.
Account controls and complaint routes
We also note the published complaints procedure and any named independent dispute service, since this differs sharply between regulatory categories.
Customer support availability
We record the support channels each casino publishes — live chat, email, telephone or help centre — and the hours they state. Where a brand does not publish response times or hours, we report that gap rather than estimating a figure we cannot support.
Operating history and stability
We consider how long a brand and its operating company have been active, whether a new casino is a genuinely new business or a new front for an existing operator, and whether terms, ownership or licensing have changed recently. Short track records are flagged, not hidden.
Frequently Asked Questions
Is it legal for a UK adult to use betting sites not on GamStop?
Playing at an overseas-licensed casino is not a criminal offence for an adult in Great Britain; the licensing obligation falls on the operator, not the customer. The important distinction is that a site accepting British customers is not the same as a site authorised by the UK Gambling Commission to serve them. If an operator is not UKGC-licensed, you fall outside the Commission's consumer protections and its complaints framework, and any dispute is handled under the rules of the overseas regulator named on the site.
Are non GamStop casinos safe to use?
No gambling site can be described as completely safe, and we do not make that claim about any brand on this page. What you can assess is the evidence: a clearly named licensing authority and licence number, an identifiable operating company, published terms that match the advertised offer, a documented complaints route and working account controls. Sites that hide any of those details carry more risk, and even well-documented casinos can delay a payout while verification is completed.
Do casinos not on GamStop really skip identity verification?
Treat "no KYC" marketing with caution. Most offshore operators run identity checks at some point, usually when you request a withdrawal, when cumulative turnover crosses a threshold, or when payment behaviour triggers an anti-money-laundering review. Some sites allow deposits and play before verification, which is what the claim usually means in practice. Source-of-funds requests — payslips, bank statements, proof of a large win elsewhere — are also common on larger withdrawals.
Can I keep an account in pounds and use PayPal?
GBP account support varies. Some gambling sites not on GamStop offer sterling wallets, while others settle in euros or US dollars and convert at a rate they set, which quietly reduces the value of both deposits and withdrawals. PayPal is the harder one: it is widely used in the UK but is not automatically available at every casino, and availability for deposits does not guarantee availability for withdrawals. Check the cashier page for your own account rather than assuming.
Are instant withdrawals realistic?
Rarely in the literal sense. A payout has two stages: the casino's own review and approval, then settlement by the payment provider. Crypto and e-wallet payouts often settle within hours once approved, while cards typically take one to three working days and bank transfers up to five. Pending periods, weekend processing gaps, first-time verification and withdrawal caps all add time. Any site promising guaranteed instant payouts in every case is overstating what it controls.
What happens when my GAMSTOP exclusion period ends?
GAMSTOP registrations run for a minimum of six months, one year or five years.
When the minimum period expires the exclusion does not switch off automatically — it continues until you contact GAMSTOP, confirm you want it lifted and complete a cooling-off period before access to UKGC-licensed sites resumes.
If you are still within an active exclusion, the right step is support rather than an alternative site.
Can I self-exclude from an individual casino not on GamStop?
Usually yes, through the responsible gambling or account settings section, but the scope is narrower than GAMSTOP.
Check whether an exclusion also blocks any linked sportsbook sharing your wallet.
For broader cover, device and bank-level blocking software and bank gambling blocks work independently of any individual casino.
What should I do if a payout is delayed or refused?
Start with the operator's own complaints procedure, in writing, quoting your account reference, the withdrawal date and amount, and any documents already supplied. Keep timestamps and screenshots. If the casino does not resolve it within its stated timeframe, escalate to the licensing authority named in the site footer or any alternative dispute resolution service it lists. Be aware that escalation routes outside the UK Gambling Commission's scope vary considerably in how quickly and how far they can intervene.

Bookies Not On Gamstop is an independent research and comparison site covering online betting sites not on GamStop. We publish reviews, bonus breakdowns, payment guides and explainers for UK adults who want to understand how these operators actually work — what the headline offers really require, how withdrawals are handled, and what protections do and do not apply once a site sits outside the UK Gambling Commission's remit.
This page explains who the site is for, how we assess operators, how we are funded, and the limits of what we can verify. Everything here was last reviewed on 4 November 2026.
What this site sets out to answer
Most people arrive with one of a few questions: why a site accepts them when they have self-excluded, whether the bonus they have seen advertised is realistic, how quickly money comes back out, and what happens if something goes wrong. Those are the questions our pages are built around.
Bonus terms, not bonus headlines. A 500% match means little without the wagering multiple, the maximum bonus bet, the expiry window and the cashout cap beside it.
Payments in practice. Whether GBP accounts are offered, whether a debit card actually processes for British customers, and where currency conversion quietly eats into a balance.
Withdrawal reality. Processing times, weekly and monthly limits, KYC and source-of-funds checks, and what to do when a payout stalls.
Regulatory standing. Which overseas licence an operator holds, who owns it, and what that means for complaints.
How we are funded
We earn commission when a reader signs up with some of the operators listed here. That is how the site pays for itself, and you should read every page with that in mind. Two things follow from it, and we hold to both:
Commercial arrangements do not buy a position. Ranking comes from our own assessment criteria, applied the same way to partnered and non-partnered sites.
Drawbacks stay in. If an operator we earn from has a punishing wagering requirement or a low monthly withdrawal ceiling, we say so in the write-up rather than burying it.
Our ratings are editorial scores produced by us. They are not customer-review averages, and they are not evidence of anyone's experience but our own research.
How we research and rank operators
We have no testing evidence: we do not open accounts, deposit funds, place bets or request withdrawals. Everything we publish comes from reading operator terms and conditions, licence registers, ownership disclosures, payment pages and software-provider listings, then comparing them against each other. Where a claim is advertising rather than verified fact, we label it as advertising.
Licensing and ownership. We look for a named licensing authority — Curaçao is the most common for this sector — and for a company name and registration behind the brand. An operator that names neither is a red flag we report.
Bonus mechanics. Wagering multiple, whether it applies to bonus or deposit plus bonus, game contribution rates, maximum stake while a bonus is active, expiry, and any cap on what can be withdrawn from bonus winnings.
Banking for UK customers. Minimum deposits, GBP support, debit cards, bank transfers, e-wallets, Paysafecard where offered, and cryptocurrency. PayPal is rarely available outside UKGC-licensed sites, so we check rather than assume.
Withdrawals. Stated processing times, limits per transaction and per period, fees, and the verification documents required before a first payout.
Games and providers. Breadth of slots, live dealer coverage, table games and jackpots, and which studios supply them.
Sportsbook, where one exists. Market depth, in-play coverage, cash-out, bet builders and whether the wallet is shared with the casino.
Support and complaints. Contact channels, published hours, and whether any independent dispute route is named.
Responsible gambling tools. Deposit and loss limits, session reminders, and account self-exclusion on the operator's own system.
Scores are reviewed when terms change. Bonus offers in particular move frequently, so always confirm the current terms on the operator's own site before depositing.
Three of the operators we cover, and what we flag about them
Our full comparison sits on the non GamStop casinos top list. The examples below show the level of detail we apply and the kind of limitation we insist on publishing.
RagnaBet — our highest-rated listing
RagnaBet holds our top editorial score of 10.0, largely on the breadth of its welcome package: an advertised 420% up to £15,000 plus 440 free spins. It is one of the few in our list quoting a sterling ceiling rather than euros, which matters if you want to avoid conversion costs on every deposit and withdrawal. Limitation: a bonus of that size is almost always paired with a high wagering multiple and a maximum bonus bet, and the £15,000 figure is a theoretical ceiling that requires a very large deposit to approach. Read the bonus terms in full; the realistic value for a typical deposit is a fraction of the headline.
Kikibet — sterling-denominated, mid-sized package
Kikibet scores 9.8 and advertises 350% up to £5,555 with 300 free spins. The appeal here is proportion: a smaller headline that a normal deposit can engage with more meaningfully than a five-figure cap. Limitation: free-spin allocations of this size are usually released in daily tranches on specific titles, with separate winnings caps, so the 300 spins are not a lump sum you control.
Betmica — the largest advertised percentage match
Betmica, also rated 9.8, leads with 570% up to £5,700 plus 270 free spins. The percentage is the highest sterling-quoted match in our list, and the cap is set at a level a mid-range depositor could actually use. Limitation: the higher the match percentage, the more bonus credit there is to clear, and clearing is where most players fall short. Check the game contribution table before assuming table games or live dealer play will count.
Betninja — flat-value alternative
Betninja (9.8) takes a different route with a £1,000 bonus and 100 free spins for all new players. Simpler terms are easier to assess, which is why it earns a place here. Limitation: the ceiling is modest next to the rest of the list, and "all new players" still means the standard eligibility, minimum deposit and verification conditions apply.

How the money works at sites like these
Taking part costs whatever you deposit — there is no entry fee, but a welcome bonus is never free money, because it requires a qualifying deposit of your own and carries wagering before anything can be withdrawn. Typical minimum deposits sit in the £10 to £20 range, though some crypto-first sites set their own floors.
Debit cards — usually instant to deposit. Acceptance for UK cards varies by operator and can change without notice.
E-wallets — generally the fastest withdrawal route when supported. PayPal is uncommon outside UKGC-licensed sites; verify before relying on it.
Bank transfer — slower, often several working days, and sometimes the only route for larger payouts.
Prepaid vouchers such as Paysafecard — deposit only; you will need a different method to withdraw.
Cryptocurrency — fast and widely offered here, but the value of your balance moves with the market and conversion spreads apply.
Expect withdrawal limits expressed per day, week or month, and expect identity verification before the first payout: photo ID, proof of address and, for larger sums, source-of-funds documentation. Pending periods, processing fees and conversion charges all shrink the amount that lands. If a payout stalls, the operator's own complaints procedure is the first step, followed by whatever dispute body its licence names.
What these sites offer beyond slots
The casino floor is the core: video slots across a range of RTP and volatility profiles, progressive jackpot titles, and classic table games. Live dealer rooms run blackjack, roulette and baccarat from studio feeds, usually with higher table minimums than the digital versions. Most of the catalogue is mobile-ready in the browser rather than through an app.
Alongside the casino, many of these operators run a sportsbook on the same account and a shared wallet — pre-match and in-play markets, accumulators, bet builders, cash-out and a growing esports section. Sports promotions work differently from casino bonuses: free bets usually carry minimum qualifying odds, often around 1.80 in decimal terms, and the stake is rarely returned with the winnings. Some sites also run cashback and loyalty schemes that rebate a percentage of net losses, which are generally lower-friction than a match bonus but lower-value too.
Legal standing, eligibility and what it means for you
GamStop is the free self-exclusion scheme for online gambling operators licensed by the Gambling Commission in Great Britain. Registering blocks your access to those sites for your chosen period — six months, one year or five years — and it cannot be lifted early. Operators listed on this site hold overseas licences instead, most commonly from Curaçao, and are not part of that scheme, which is why registration does not stop them accepting a British customer.
Accepting UK customers is not the same as being authorised to serve them. A Curaçao licence brings different standards of oversight, different complaint routes and no access to UK dispute resolution or the Commission's consumer protections. Ownership is often held by groups registered outside the UK. We report what each operator discloses and say so plainly when disclosure is thin.
You must be 18 or over.
If you are on GamStop, the responsible course is to let the exclusion run.
Blocking software at device or bank level, plus the support services set out on our responsible gambling page, are more effective than willpower alone.
Nothing here is financial advice, and no operator can be described as completely safe. Gambling is entertainment with a built-in house edge, not income.
Corrections and getting in touch
Terms change, brands relaunch and payment options come and go. If you find something on this site that is out of date or wrong, tell us and we will check it against the source and amend it. Our contact page lists the ways to reach the editorial team, and the terms and conditions set out how the site may be used.
If you are deciding where to start, work from the terms rather than the headline: pick the offer whose wagering multiple, maximum bonus bet and withdrawal limits you could realistically live with, confirm the current conditions on the operator's own site, and set a deposit limit before your first transaction.
